newsitem.title: DUBAI: United Arab Emirates shares rise in active trade.
newsitem.headline: United Arab Emirates shares rise in active trade.

text.p: Shares on the United Arab Emirates informal stock exchange ended the week to Thursday higher in active trade which brokers attributed to a busy primary issues market.
They said trading picked up as investors were offered shares by the new Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, which is to be capitalised at one billion dirhams ($272 million).

"It is unusual for the market to see this level of activity at this time of the year. Investors are staying behind to buy into the Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank offering and other IPOs expected this summer," Zuhair Kaswani, financial analyst at the Sharjah-based al-Sharhan Stocks and Bonds, said.
The National Bank of Abu Dhabi (NBAD) index rose 19.03 points to 2,604.14 from 2,585.11.
Brokers attributed the index ascent mainly to a 10 dirham increase in market leader Etisalat. Some traders quoted Abu Dhabi National Insurance Co up at 1,125 dirhams from 1,120.
Kaswani said Emaar Properties was traded one dirham higher at 17 dirhams after the company announced a new housing project.
Emirates Bank International was traded higher. NBAD put it at 25 dirhams, while others put it 2.5 dirhams up at 26.5.
Abu Dhabi National Hotels Co gained six dirhams to 122 dirhams. NBAD put it up four dirhams at 120 dirhams.
